source_excerpts.text:
I obtained a constructive theorem showing that a rapidly mixing hidden system can require exponentially long passive observation to distinguish from equilibrium, while a specified weak-field experiment distinguishes it in polynomial time.
The passive lower bound covers the entire continuously observed trajectory, including exact transition times and unlimited computational processing. It is not merely a failure of two-point correlations or a particular inference algorithm.
The candidate new mechanism is an observation ladder: a positive stochastic realization whose hidden dynamics has only a third-order nilpotent component, but whose unforced observations must traverse an arbitrarily long algebraic sequence before exposing it. A conservative perturbation accesses a much shorter sequence.
Historical priority and independent correctness remain unestablished. The complete argument and executable constructions are supplied below. Detecting hidden dissipation from apparently time-symmetric observations is already established research; that phenomenon alone is not the novelty claim. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.08765)
For every integer \(r\ge1\), construct a rational continuous-time Markov chain \(Q_r\), with between \(4r\) and \(16r\) microscopic states, and observe only
\[ Y_t=f(X_t)\in\{-1,+1\}. \]
Compare it with an equilibrium binary chain \(Z_t\) that flips sign at rate \(1/2\).
The construction gives
\[ \boxed{ T_{\mathrm{passive}}\ge16^r-2 } \]
for distinguishing the two hypotheses with equal-prior success probability at least \(2/3\).
Under the explicitly specified field intervention below, distinguishing them with error probability at most \(\zeta\) requires only
\[ \boxed{ T_{\mathrm{active}} = O\!\left( r^6\log(1/\zeta)\,[1+\log(r/\zeta)] \right). } \]
The second bound includes sampling and waiting for the system to return close to its unperturbed stationary distribution. It does not assume free resets or an exact susceptibility oracle.
This separation holds despite benign microscopic properties:
\[ \frac{7}{8n}\le q_{ij}\le\frac{9}{8n} \qquad(i\ne j), \]
uniform stationary probabilities, mixing bounded by \(e^{-t/2}\), and every nonzero eigenvalue equal to \(-1\). There are no exponentially rare microscopic states, exponentially small rates, or metastable waiting times.

source_excerpts.text:
The central issue is to construct \(A\) so that it simultaneously produces positive transition rates, long observational concealment, and a short controlled response.
Use a uniform Boolean state space \(\Omega=\mathbb F_2^d\), with Walsh characters
\[ \chi_a(x)=(-1)^{a\cdot x}. \]
These form an orthonormal basis. Choose a character \(f\), put \(\ell=2r-1\), and choose characters \(c_1,\ldots,c_\ell\) such that
\[ 1,\ f,\ c_1,\ldots,c_\ell,\ d_1,\ldots,d_\ell, \qquad d_j=fc_j, \]
are all distinct.
Define \(A\) on this basis by
\[ Af=d_1, \qquad Ac_j=d_{j+1}\quad(1\le j<\ell), \qquad Ac_\ell=f, \tag{3} \]
and set it to zero on every other basis character.
Then
\[ A1=A^*1=0,\qquad \|A\|_{2\to2}=1,\qquad A^3=0. \]
In particular, the hidden propagator is unusually simple:
\[ \boxed{ e^{tQ_r} = J+e^{-t} \left[ I-J+\varepsilon tA+\frac{\varepsilon^2t^2}{2}A^2 \right]. } \tag{4} \]
But observation introduces another operator:
\[ Dg=fg. \]
It acts by
\[ D1=f,\quad Df=1,\quad Dc_j=d_j,\quad Dd_j=c_j. \]
Interleaving evolution and observation therefore creates the long sequence
\[ f \xrightarrow{A}d_1 \xrightarrow{D}c_1 \xrightarrow{A}d_2 \xrightarrow{D}\cdots \xrightarrow{D}c_\ell \xrightarrow{A}f. \tag{5} \]
Every closed scalar observation word containing \(A\) must use at least \(2r\) copies of \(A\). Repeated observation cannot skip a rung.
This is the relevant distinction: simple hidden time evolution does not imply shallow observable structure.
There are \(2r\) nonzero Walsh entries in \(A\). In the ordinary state basis,
\[ A_{xy} = \frac1n \sum_{\text{ladder edges }a\to b} \chi_b(x)\chi_a(y), \]
so
\[ |A_{xy}|\le\frac{2r}{n}, \qquad K:=\max_x\sum_y|A_{xy}|\le2r. \]
With \(\varepsilon=1/(16r)\), equation (2) consequently gives
\[ \frac{7}{8n}\le q_{xy}\le\frac{9}{8n} \]
off the diagonal. Zero row and column sums of \(A\) establish both the generator property and the uniform stationary law.
The construction therefore produces an actual irreducible stochastic system, not a signed representation whose physical realization is deferred.
The necessary characters and symmetry can be acquired explicitly with \(n\le16r\).

No computational-complexity assumption is involved. Even an optimal passive test with unlimited processing obeys it.
Now apply the field in equation (1).
Let
\[ \chi_r(t) = \left.\frac{d}{dh}\mathbb E_h f(X_t)\right|_{h=0}, \]
starting in the unperturbed stationary law.
Write
\[ S=\frac12(Q_r+Q_r^*). \]
Differentiating the controlled generator and using stationarity gives
\[ \chi_r(t) = -\int_0^t \langle Sf,e^{sQ_r}f\rangle_\pi\,ds. \tag{12} \]
For the ladder,
\[ Sf=-f+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}(d_1+c_\ell), \]
while
\[ e^{sQ_r}f=e^{-s}(f+\varepsilon s\,d_1). \]
Orthogonality therefore gives
\[ \langle Sf,e^{sQ_r}f\rangle_\pi = e^{-s}\left(-1+\frac{\varepsilon^2s}{2}\right). \]
Integrating,
\[ \boxed{ \chi_r(t) = 1-e^{-t} -\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2} \left[1-(1+t)e^{-t}\right]. } \tag{13} \]
At \(t=1\), the gap from the equilibrium response is
\[ \chi_{\mathrm{eq}}(1)-\chi_r(1) = c_*\varepsilon^2, \qquad c_*=\frac{1-2/e}{2}>\frac18. \tag{14} \]
The passive signal requires \(2r\) perturbative steps. The response signal appears at second order, independently of \(r\).
That is the operational role of the new construction.
Choose
\[ h=\frac{\varepsilon}{100} \]
and measure the two endpoint means \(m(+h)\), \(m(-h)\) at time one. Form
\[ D(h)=\frac{m(h)-m(-h)}{2h}. \]
For \(|h|\le1\), the first three field derivatives of the generator have sup-norm operator bounds below \(7\). The time-ordered derivative formula then bounds
\[ \left|\frac{d^3m(h)}{dh^3}\right|<500. \]
Consequently, each central difference differs from its exact susceptibility by at most \(500h^2/6\). Comparing the two hypotheses,
\[ \boxed{ D_{\mathrm{eq}}(h)-D_r(h) \ge \frac{13}{120}\varepsilon^2 > \frac{\varepsilon^2}{10}. } \tag{15} \]
The equilibrium reference is explicitly computable:
\[ m_{\mathrm{eq}}(h) = \tanh(h)\,[1-e^{-\cosh(h)}]. \]
Estimate each endpoint mean to accuracy
\[ a=\frac{h\varepsilon^2}{80} =\frac{\varepsilon^3}{8000}. \]
Hoeffding’s inequality gives a sufficient sample count per field sign
\[ N= \left\lceil \frac{2}{a^2}\log\frac8\zeta \right\rceil = O\!\left(r^6\log(1/\zeta)\right). \tag{16} \]
Before each trial, turn off the field and wait
\[ L\ge2\log(8N/\zeta). \]
